//: Why this project exists: `apps/node/tsconfig.json` includes only `src/**/*.ts`, so `tsc -b` never sees the test tree and a type error in a test cannot be a compile error. This project checks the node tests. It is deliberately NOT `composite` and NOT referenced from the root `tsconfig.json`: the tests import `../src/**`, which drags the whole product graph into the program, and build mode would then demand that every one of those files be listed in this project (TS6307) and would recompile them. A plain `tsc -p` program checks the tests plus whatever they import, without claiming to own the product build. It is invoked explicitly by `npm run typecheck` (`tsc -b && npm run typecheck:tests`) and by the CI node-refactor job — the same shape EnvoyCoder uses for its `tsconfig.unchecked.json`.
//paths: `paths: {}` overrides the base config's `src` mappings so workspace packages resolve through their built declarations (the surface a consumer sees) instead of their sources. With the `src` mappings a test that reaches a package *subpath* (`@envoymesh/api/approval-queue`) resolves to `dist/` while the package root resolves to `src/`, and TypeScript then reports phantom `private property` clashes; it also re-checks `packages/vault/src` without `packages/vault`'s ambient `declare module` files. `tsc -b` builds the declarations first (see the `typecheck` script), so this is current.
//scope: This is still a seed, not the whole `apps/node/test` tree. As widened 2026-09-17, it covers 164 files: every *directory* and every multi-file *filename-prefix glob* under `apps/node/test` whose files and transitive import closure were at 0 errors under these exact settings — measured, not guessed. `apps/node/test` itself is flat (657 files), so the root is covered by `home-*.ts`-style globs; there is no all-clean root directory to add. The 967 remaining errors across 234 files, their dominant classes and the per-file checklist live in `docs/node-test-typecheck-debt.md`. Adding a new glob/file here is safe only if its whole transitive import closure is clean: this program reports errors in imported files too, so one stale helper can turn a green glob red. Measured with `tsconfig.test.measure.json`, which extends this file and widens `include` to `apps/node/test/**/*.ts`, compiled by `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.measure.json --pretty false`.
